findings.finding: Fault classes are imbalanced: Container Hardware has 83 cases and Node Memory only 9 (ratio 9.2:1).

6 nodes have no trace features and 16 have no log features in any training sample (structural absence, not missing values); overall 81% of metric entries are exactly 0 (zero equals the series mean after ARMOR's scaling - inferred, so a zero is not a missing value).
12 channel pairs have |r| >= 0.95 on system-level training series (38 channels are constant and excluded); mean |r| within metrics is 0.15.

Root-cause-node deviation relative to other nodes (mean |value| ratio, training cases): metric 1.45 before vs 3.56 after injection; trace 0.92 before vs 1.94 after injection; log 1.04 before vs 1.70 after injection. Service-level cases average over all replicas of the named service.

37 channels are constant in the training partition. Heaviest tails: transport_closing_warning (3.3% of values beyond |3|), kpi_container_network_receive_MB (2.9% of values beyond |3|), duration (1.5% of values beyond |3|).

On the approved Model 1 split, 0 of 130 channels differ between training and validation by KS >= 0.2 (largest: kpi_container_memory_cache, KS 0.13). Diagnostic only: nothing is tuned on validation, and KS on pooled entries is sensitive to the large zero mass.

Model-development statistics (scaler, structural masks, histograms, correlations, outliers, incident ratios on train cases) use only the approved Model 1 train period; the validation period appears only in the diagnostic train-vs-validation comparison; temporal trends, descriptive stats and held-out-case rows are full-dataset descriptive views and are labelled as such.
